requirements.text: The warehouse must record every vendor, being a company from which goods are purchased.
A vendor is identified in business terms by its vendor account number, the identification number by which purchasing staff and vendor correspondence refer to the company.
The warehouse must retain the internal business entity identifier of each vendor in addition to the vendor account number, because other purchasing records point to the internal identifier.
The warehouse must record the vendor's company name and make it reportable.
Each vendor carries a credit rating on a five-point scale: Superior, Excellent, Above average, Average, Below average.
Reporting must present the vendor credit rating in its business wording, not as a bare code.
Each vendor carries a preferred vendor status that is either 'preferred over other vendors supplying the same product' or 'do not use if another vendor is available'.
Purchasing management must be able to see whether orders are in fact being placed with preferred vendors.
requirements.obj: purchase orders placed with preferred vendors

requirements.text: Each vendor carries an active flag indicating whether the vendor is still actively used or is no longer used.
Vendors that are no longer used must remain in the warehouse so that historical orders placed with them stay reportable.
Where a vendor offers an electronic purchasing interface, the warehouse must record the purchasing web service address.
Reporting must tolerate the absence of the purchasing web service address, as the attribute is not always populated.
The warehouse must retain the history of changes to vendor attributes, in particular credit rating, preferred status and active flag.
The warehouse must allow the state of a vendor at the time an order was placed to be reconstructed, not only its current state.
The warehouse must record, for each combination of a product and a vendor, the standing commercial terms under which the product is bought from that vendor.
The same product may be supplied by several vendors, and a vendor may supply several products.
The supply relationship is identified in business terms by the pairing of the product and the vendor.
The warehouse must record the average lead time, being the average span of time in days between placing an order with the vendor and receiving the purchased product.
The warehouse must record the standard price, being the vendor's usual selling price for the product.
The warehouse must record the last receipt cost, being the selling price when the product was last purchased from the vendor.
The warehouse must record the last receipt date, being the date the product was last received from the vendor.
The warehouse must record the agreed minimum and maximum order quantities for the product from the vendor so that buyers and reporting can see whether orders respect the agreed bounds.

Which field carries the minimum and which the maximum order quantity meaning must be confirmed with the purchasing team before either is used in reporting or any threshold check, because the source descriptions are transposed.
requirements.obj: minimum and maximum order quantity fields

requirements.text: The quantity currently on order for the product from the vendor must be available as an indicator of open commitment.
The warehouse must record the unit of measure in which the product is bought from the vendor.
Quantities and prices must always be interpreted together with the unit of measure, since the same product may be bought in different units from different vendors.
The warehouse must retain the history of supply terms (prices, lead times, quantity bounds) so that trends in agreed price and lead time per vendor and product can be analysed.
Reporting must be clear about whether it shows the current value or the value as at a point in time for running values such as quantity on order and last receipt figures.
The warehouse must be able to identify each purchased product consistently and join purchasing activity to the wider product information maintained outside the purchasing area.
The warehouse must record every purchase order placed with a vendor.
A purchase order is identified in business terms by its purchase order number.
Each purchase order is placed with exactly one vendor.
Each purchase order is created by one employee, the buyer who raised it.
The warehouse must be able to report purchasing activity by the employee who created the order.
Employee name, department and role are not available in the purchasing area and must come from the HR/employee area if the business wants to report on them.
Each purchase order names a shipping method, being the shipping company and rate agreement used to bring the goods to the business.
Each purchase order carries an order date, the date the order was created.
Each purchase order carries an estimated shipment date, the date the vendor is expected to ship.
The business must be able to compare the estimated shipment date against actual receipt activity.
requirements.obj: estimated shipment date with actual receipt activity

requirements.text: Each purchase order carries a status that is one of Pending, Approved, Rejected or Complete.
Reporting must present the purchase order status in business wording.
The business must be able to see the population of orders in each status, in particular orders that are approved but not yet complete.
Each purchase order carries a revision number, an incrementing counter tracking how the order has changed over time.
The business must be able to know whether an order was revised and how many times.
The warehouse must retain the history of a purchase order as it changes, so that status transitions and revisions are traceable over time and not overwritten by the latest state.
requirements.obj: purchase order status transitions and revisions

requirements.text: The business must be able to answer when an order was approved and how long it sat pending.
requirements.obj: purchase order approval timing and pending duration

requirements.text: The business expectation for revision history reconstruction must be agreed, because the source holds only the current order version with its revision number and last-updated date and its reconstruction depends on source capture frequency.
Each purchase order carries financial totals: a subtotal (the sum of the value of its lines), a tax amount, a freight amount, and a total due to the vendor (subtotal plus tax plus freight).
The business must be able to analyse purchasing spend by vendor, by employee, by shipping method, and over time, using the order totals.
The warehouse must be able to demonstrate that the reported order totals are consistent with the underlying order lines.
Any discrepancy between the stated order total and the sum of its lines must be visible to the business as a finding.
requirements.obj: discrepancy between order total and sum of lines

requirements.text: Freight and tax are order-level charges and are not attributed to individual products in the source.
If product-level landed cost is wanted, the business must decide the basis for allocating freight and tax across order lines, as it cannot be derived from the source.
Each purchase order contains one or more lines, one per purchased product.
A purchase order line is identified in business terms by the purchase order it belongs to together with its line number.
Each purchase order line refers to exactly one product.
Each purchase order line carries the quantity ordered.
Each purchase order line carries the unit price, which is the vendor's selling price for a single unit of the product on this order.
Each purchase order line carries a line total, which is the ordered quantity multiplied by the unit price.
Each purchase order line carries a due date, the date on which the product is expected to be received.
Delivery-performance analysis must work at line level, not only at order level, because due dates are held per line and different products on the same order may be expected at different times.
The business must be able to compare the unit price actually paid on a line with the standard price agreed for that product and vendor, in order to identify off-contract purchasing.
requirements.obj: unit price paid with standard price

requirements.text: Each purchase order line records the quantity actually received from the vendor.
Each purchase order line records the quantity rejected during inspection.
Each purchase order line records the quantity accepted into inventory, being the received quantity less the rejected quantity.
The business must be able to measure the fulfilment gap between ordered and received quantity, including under-delivery and over-delivery, per line, per order, per product and per vendor.
The business must be able to measure inspection reject rates, being rejected quantity as a share of received quantity, by vendor and by product, as the primary indicator of incoming quality.

The warehouse must retain the progression of received and rejected quantities per line over the life of the order, so that the quantity received as at a given date can be answered and partial deliveries are visible.
requirements.obj: history of received and rejected quantities

requirements.text: The source records only cumulative received, rejected and accepted quantities per line with a last-updated date, and does not record individual receipt events, receipt dates or inspection outcomes per delivery; analysis of individual deliveries requires another source or the requirement must be dropped.
The business must be able to compare the due date on a line against evidence of actual receipt in order to measure on-time delivery by vendor.
requirements.obj: line due date with actual receipt timing

requirements.text: The last receipt date held on the vendor–product supply relationship is currently the only available measure of actual receipt timing, and its sufficiency as a basis for an on-time-delivery metric must be agreed with the business.

The business must be able to compare actual elapsed time from order to receipt against the average lead time recorded for that vendor and product, to validate whether recorded lead times are realistic.
requirements.obj: actual elapsed time with average lead time

requirements.text: The warehouse must record every shipping method available for inbound purchases.
A shipping method is identified in business terms by the shipping company name.
A shipping method has an internal shipping method identifier that is used on purchase orders.
Each shipping method carries a minimum shipping charge (ship base).
Each shipping method carries a charge per pound (ship rate).
The business must be able to analyse freight cost by shipping method.
The business must be able to compare the freight actually charged on orders against the base and per-pound rates agreed with the shipping company.
requirements.obj: freight charged with agreed shipping rates

requirements.text: The warehouse must retain the history of ship base and ship rate so that freight charged on a historical order can be assessed against the rates in force at that time.
requirements.obj: history of ship base and ship rate

requirements.text: The technical replication identifier on shipping method records in the source has no business meaning and is not required for reporting.
A vendor supplies one or more products, and a product may be supplied by more than one vendor.
Each vendor–product supply relationship carries its own agreed price, lead time and order quantity bounds.
A purchase order is placed with exactly one vendor.
A purchase order is created by one employee.
A purchase order specifies one shipping method.
Receipt and inspection outcomes attach to the purchase order line, not to the order as a whole.
Products on order lines are normally, but not necessarily, products with a recorded supply relationship with that vendor.
Where a line names a product with no recorded supply relationship for that vendor, this must be surfaced as a finding rather than hidden as a data error.
requirements.obj: order lines without a supply relationship

requirements.text: The warehouse must use the last-modified date and time carried by every purchasing source record to establish when information changed.
The warehouse must not present a value as current when a more recent change exists.

All monetary amounts in the purchasing area are held in a single currency in the source with no currency indicator, and the currency of purchase orders and prices must be clarified if vendors in other currencies are used.
Codes with defined business meanings, namely purchase order status, vendor credit rating, preferred vendor status and active flag, must be presented in reporting in their business wording.
The mapping of codes to business wording must be held once and applied consistently.
Quantities must always be interpreted together with the unit of measure recorded on the relevant vendor–product supply relationship.
Reporting must prevent aggregation of quantities across products or units of measure without regard to the unit.
requirements.obj: aggregation of quantities across units of measure

requirements.text: Records that no longer represent current operational reality, such as inactive vendors, completed or rejected orders and discontinued supply relationships, must be retained in full.
Nothing may be physically removed because it has ceased to be current.

business_keys.rationale: REQ-002 explicitly states a vendor is identified in business terms by its vendor account number, used by purchasing staff and in vendor correspondence (recognised, unique, business-used).

REQ-003 requires retaining the internal identifier because other purchasing records (e.g. purchase orders) reference it; it is system-assigned so a weaker business key than the account number, but needed for joining.
REQ-004 records the company name as a reportable attribute only; names are not guaranteed unique or stable, so it is a poor key.

REQ-029 requires identifying each purchased product consistently and joining to product information held outside purchasing; ProductID appears on ProductVendor and PurchaseOrderDetail as the shared identifier. Not explicitly called unique, and it is probably system-assigned.
REQ-017 states the supply relationship is identified in business terms by the pairing of product and vendor (REQ-015, REQ-016, REQ-029-2); the composite is unique per relationship and not nullable.
REQ-031 states a purchase order is identified in business terms by its purchase order number; it is referenced by order lines (REQ-002-2), stable and unique.

business_keys.field: PurchaseOrderID + PurchaseOrderDetailID (purchase order with line number)
business_keys.rationale: REQ-002-2 states a line is identified by the purchase order it belongs to together with its line number; the composite is unique and non-null.
On its own the line number is a system-generated detail identifier; REQ-002-2 requires it to be combined with the purchase order, so it is weak alone.
REQ-021-2 states a shipping method is identified in business terms by the shipping company name; this is the business-recognised, unique identifier.
REQ-022-2 notes an internal identifier used on purchase orders (REQ-036, REQ-033-2); it is a system-generated surrogate, so it scores low as a business key although it is needed for references.

REQ-033 and REQ-034 require each purchase order to be tied to its creating employee for reporting; PurchaseOrderHeader carries EmployeeID. Employee master data sits in the HR area (REQ-035), so the key is only a reference here and no business identifier is stated.

hubs.name: hub_address
hubs.description: Postal address recorded once and shareable by many parties.

hubs.name: hub_address_type
hubs.description: Reference list of address types (Billing, Home, Shipping).

hubs.name: hub_contact_type
hubs.description: Reference list of contact roles.

hubs.name: hub_phone_number_type

hubs.name: hub_state_province

hubs.name: hub_department

hubs.name: hub_shift

hubs.name: hub_job_candidate
hubs.description: Job candidates whose applications are held by HR.

hubs.name: hub_product

The hub is therefore anchored on ProductID so those relations can attach, and ProductNumber is kept as a descriptive attribute.

hubs.name: hub_product_category
hubs.description: Top level of the merchandising hierarchy. Anchored on the ID because ProductSubcategory references categories by ID; Name is kept in a satellite.

hubs.name: hub_product_subcategory
hubs.description: Second level of the merchandising hierarchy. Anchored on the ID because Product references subcategories by ID; Name is kept in a satellite.

hubs.name: hub_product_model
hubs.description: Product model shared by several products. Anchored on the ID because Product and the association tables reference models by ID; Name is kept in a satellite.

hubs.name: hub_culture
hubs.description: Language/locale designation, identified by a short culture code.

hubs.name: hub_unit_measure
hubs.description: Standard unit of measure, identified by a short code.

hubs.name: hub_product_description
hubs.description: Free-text marketing description held in a library, independent of any one product.

hubs.name: hub_product_photo
hubs.description: Photograph in the product photo library.

hubs.name: hub_illustration
hubs.description: Technical diagram used in manufacturing instructions.

hubs.name: hub_document
hubs.description: Entry (document or folder) in the hierarchical controlled document library.

hubs.name: hub_location
hubs.description: Manufacturing location / inventory location. Anchored on the ID because inventory and routing reference locations by ID; Name is kept in a satellite.

hubs.name: hub_scrap_reason
hubs.description: Standard scrap reason. Anchored on the ID because WorkOrder references scrap reasons by ID.

hubs.name: hub_work_order
hubs.description: Work order raised to manufacture a product.

hubs.name: hub_inventory_transaction
hubs.description: Inventory transaction (stock movement), fed by both the live and the archive store so they form one continuous history.

hubs.name: hub_product_review
hubs.description: Customer review of a product.

hubs.name: hub_purchase_order
hubs.description: Purchase order placed with a vendor, identified by its purchase order number.

hubs.name: hub_purchase_order_line
hubs.description: A purchase order line, identified by its purchase order together with its line number. Receipt and inspection outcomes attach to the line.

hubs.name: hub_ship_method
hubs.description: Shipping method (shipping company and rate agreement) used for inbound purchases. Keyed on ShipMethodID, the identifier purchase orders carry, so orders can join to it. The shipping company name is kept in the satellite.

links.name: link_business_entity_address
links.description: Which addresses a party uses and in what capacity; party+address+type is unique.

links.name: link_business_entity_contact
links.description: Organisation (business entity) to the person acting as its contact, in a contact role; organisation+person+role is unique.

links.name: link_business_entity_phone_number_type
links.description: A person's telephone numbers qualified by phone number type.

links.name: link_address_state_province
links.description: The state or province in which an address sits (country derived via state).

links.name: link_state_province_country_region
links.description: Each state or province belongs to exactly one country or region.

links.name: link_business_entity_department_shift
links.description: Employee assignment to a department and a shift over time, from EmployeeDepartmentHistory. An effectivity satellite tracks the start and end dates for each employee.
links.unit_of_work: BusinessEntityID + DepartmentID + ShiftID (assignment starting at StartDate)

links.name: link_business_entity_job_candidate
links.description: Links a candidate record to the employee hired from it. If this link exists, the applicant was hired.

links.name: link_product_product_subcategory
links.description: A product belongs to at most one subcategory. The link is optional.

links.name: link_product_subcategory_product_category
links.description: A subcategory belongs to exactly one category.

links.name: link_product_model_description_culture

links.name: link_product_model_illustration
links.description: Many-to-many association of illustrations with product models.

links.name: link_product_product_photo
links.description: Many-to-many association of products with photographs.

links.name: link_product_document
links.description: Many-to-many association of products with documents.

links.name: link_document_business_entity
links.description: Document owner. The owner is an employee held in the existing HR hub (Document.Owner maps to BusinessEntityID).

links.name: link_product_location
links.description: Inventory: a product held at a location (many-to-many).

links.name: link_work_order_product
links.description: The product a work order manufactures.

links.name: link_work_order_scrap_reason
links.description: Scrap reason recorded on a work order. The link is optional.

links.name: link_work_order_product_location
links.description: Work order routing: operations of a work order for a product, performed at a manufacturing location.
links.unit_of_work: WorkOrderID + ProductID + LocationID (operation sequence as dependent key)

links.name: link_inventory_transaction_product
links.description: The product moved by an inventory transaction.

links.name: link_product_review_product
links.description: The product a review relates to.

links.name: link_product_vendor
links.description: Supply relationship between a product and the vendor (business entity) that supplies it, together with the unit of measure the product is bought in. Many-to-many.
links.unit_of_work: ProductID + vendor BusinessEntityID (+ UnitMeasureCode) from ProductVendor

links.name: link_purchase_order_vendor_employee_ship_method
links.description: Purchase order header relationship: each order is placed with one vendor, created by one employee and shipped by one shipping method. Vendor and employee are both business entities, so each takes part under its own role.
links.unit_of_work: PurchaseOrderID + VendorID + EmployeeID + ShipMethodID from PurchaseOrderHeader

links.name: link_purchase_order_line_product
links.description: Places each purchase order line in its order and ties it to the one product it refers to.

links.name: link_purchase_order_business_entity
links.description: Declared foreign key PurchaseOrderHeader.EmployeeID references BUSINESSENTITYID; ratified from the source catalogue (WP34).

satellites.description: Geographic coordinates of the address.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_line_details
satellites.description: Ordered terms of a purchase order line: due date, ordered quantity, unit price and line total.
satellites.split_rationale: Terms fixed when the order is placed, which rarely change afterwards.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_line_receipt
satellites.description: Cumulative received, rejected and accepted (stocked) quantities per line. History is kept so the quantity received as at a date, and partial deliveries, are visible.
satellites.split_rationale: Receipt progression that changes with each delivery. Holds the single ModifiedDate for PurchaseOrderDetail.

satellites.name: sat_ship_method_details
satellites.description: Shipping company name and agreed ship base and ship rate, with history kept so historical freight can be checked against the rates then in force. The rowguid replication identifier is left out.

contracts.name: ProductVendor

schema.name: ProductID

schema.name: BusinessEntityID

schema.name: AverageLeadTime
schema.description: Average lead time between placing a purchase order and receiving the product from the vendor.

schema.name: StandardPrice
schema.description: Standard price of the product quoted by the vendor.

schema.name: LastReceiptCost
schema.description: Unit cost of the product at the most recent receipt from the vendor.

schema.name: LastReceiptDate
schema.description: Date the product was last received from the vendor.

schema.name: MinOrderQty
schema.description: Minimum quantity that can be ordered from the vendor for this product.

schema.name: MaxOrderQty
schema.description: Maximum quantity that can be ordered from the vendor for this product.

schema.name: OnOrderQty
schema.description: Quantity currently on order from the vendor for this product.

schema.name: UnitMeasureCode
schema.description: Code of the unit of measure used for the product's standard quantities with this vendor.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the record was last modified in the source.

contracts.name: PurchaseOrderDetail

schema.name: PurchaseOrderID
schema.description: Identifier of the parent purchase order (references PurchaseOrderHeader).

schema.name: PurchaseOrderDetailID
schema.description: Identifier of the individual line item within the purchase order detail.

schema.name: DueDate
schema.description: Date the ordered product is expected to be delivered.

schema.name: OrderQty
schema.description: Quantity of the product ordered on this line.

schema.name: ProductID
schema.description: Identifier of the product being ordered.

schema.name: UnitPrice
schema.description: Price per unit of the product at the time of ordering.

schema.name: LineTotal
schema.description: Line total for the line item (order quantity multiplied by unit price).

schema.name: ReceivedQty
schema.description: Quantity of the product actually received from the vendor.

schema.name: RejectedQty
schema.description: Quantity of the product rejected on inspection.

schema.name: StockedQty
schema.description: Quantity of the product accepted into stock.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source row was last modified.

contracts.name: PurchaseOrderHeader
contracts.doc: Purchase order header records from the source system, one row per purchase order, covering vendor, ship method, order and ship dates, and monetary totals. schema.name: PurchaseOrderID
schema.description: Unique identifier of the purchase order (business key).

schema.name: RevisionNumber
schema.description: Revision number of the purchase order, tracking changes to the order.

schema.name: Status
schema.description: Status code of the purchase order. The allowed value set is not defined in the requirements.

schema.name: EmployeeID
schema.description: Identifier of the employee who created the purchase order.

schema.name: VendorID
schema.description: Identifier of the vendor the order is placed with; corresponds to Vendor.BusinessEntityID.

schema.name: ShipMethodID
schema.description: Identifier of the shipping method used; corresponds to ShipMethod.ShipMethodID.

schema.name: OrderDate
schema.description: Date the purchase order was created.

schema.name: ShipDate
schema.description: Date the order was or is expected to be shipped. May be absent for orders not yet shipped.

schema.name: SubTotal
schema.description: Order subtotal in currency units, before tax and freight.

schema.name: TaxAmt
schema.description: Tax amount applied to the purchase order.

schema.name: Freight
schema.description: Shipping/freight charge for the purchase order.

schema.name: TotalDue
schema.description: Total amount due for the order (subtotal plus tax and freight).

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the record was last modified in the source.

contracts.name: ShipMethod
contracts.doc: Shipping methods available for purchase orders, sourced from the ShipMethod source table into staging. The contract enforces the declared schema and the business key (ShipMethodID); value-level checks are advisory unless a requirement mandates otherwise. Ownership and agreement are to be confirmed at the human-in-the-loop checkpoint.

schema.name: ShipMethodID
schema.description: Unique identifier of the shipping method; business key of the asset and referenced by purchase order headers.

schema.name: Name
schema.description: Name of the shipping method.

schema.name: ShipBase
schema.description: Minimum shipping charge for the shipping method.

schema.name: ShipRate
schema.description: Shipping charge per unit of measure (e.g. per weight) for the shipping method.

schema.name: rowguid
schema.description: Globally unique identifier (GUID) for the row, used by the source system for row identification.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the source record was last modified.

contracts.name: Vendor
contracts.doc: Vendor represents a supplier from which the organization purchases goods, identified by BusinessEntityID, as landed from the source into staging. The contract enforces the declared schema and key/not-null constraints; value-level semantics are minimal pending producer/consumer review.

schema.name: BusinessEntityID
schema.description: Unique identifier of the vendor business entity; business key of the Vendor asset.

schema.name: AccountNumber
schema.description: Vendor account number used to identify the vendor in purchasing.

schema.name: Name
schema.description: Name of the vendor company.

schema.name: CreditRating
schema.description: Credit rating assigned to the vendor. Allowed values and scale are not specified in the requirements.

schema.name: PreferredVendorStatus
schema.description: Indicates whether the vendor is a preferred vendor. Value representation is not specified in the requirements.

schema.name: ActiveFlag
schema.description: Indicates whether the vendor is currently active. Value representation is not specified in the requirements.

schema.name: PurchasingWebServiceURL
schema.description: URL of the vendor's purchasing web service, if any.

schema.name: ModifiedDate
schema.description: Date and time the vendor record was last modified in the source.

# ADR-0001: Data Vault model derived from requirements

**Status:** Proposed
**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Decision makers:** Vault-Agent (generated) — pending human review

## Context

This model was derived automatically by the Vault-Agent pipeline from 98 requirement(s) and 11 business key candidate(s). It records the Data Vault 2.0 structures the modeler chose and traces each back to the requirements that justify it.

## Decision

Model the following Data Vault 2.0 structures.

### Hubs (3)

- **hub_purchase_order** — business key `PurchaseOrderID`. Purchase order placed with a vendor, identified by its purchase order number. _(requirements: REQ-030, REQ-031, REQ-044-2, REQ-045-2)_
- **hub_purchase_order_line** — business key `purchase_order_line`. A purchase order line, identified by its purchase order together with its line number. Receipt and inspection outcomes attach to the line. _(requirements: REQ-001-2, REQ-002-2, REQ-034-2, REQ-008-2)_
- **hub_ship_method** — business key `ShipMethodID`. Shipping method (shipping company and rate agreement) used for inbound purchases. Keyed on ShipMethodID, the identifier purchase orders carry, so orders can join to it. The shipping company name is kept in the satellite. _(requirements: REQ-020-2, REQ-021-2, REQ-022-2, REQ-036)_

### Links (4)

- **link_product_vendor** — connects hub_product, hub_business_entity (vendor), hub_unit_measure. Supply relationship between a product and the vendor (business entity) that supplies it, together with the unit of measure the product is bought in. Many-to-many. Unit of work: ProductID + vendor BusinessEntityID (+ UnitMeasureCode) from ProductVendor. _(requirements: REQ-015, REQ-016, REQ-017, REQ-025, REQ-026, REQ-029, REQ-029-2, REQ-042-2)_
- **link_purchase_order_vendor_employee_ship_method** — connects hub_purchase_order, hub_business_entity (vendor), hub_business_entity (employee), hub_ship_method. Purchase order header relationship: each order is placed with one vendor, created by one employee and shipped by one shipping method. Vendor and employee are both business entities, so each takes part under its own role. Unit of work: PurchaseOrderID + VendorID + EmployeeID + ShipMethodID from PurchaseOrderHeader. _(requirements: REQ-032, REQ-033, REQ-034, REQ-035, REQ-036, REQ-049, REQ-031-2, REQ-032-2, REQ-033-2)_
- **link_purchase_order_line_product** — connects hub_purchase_order_line, hub_purchase_order, hub_product. Places each purchase order line in its order and ties it to the one product it refers to. Unit of work: PurchaseOrderID + PurchaseOrderDetailID + ProductID from PurchaseOrderDetail. _(requirements: REQ-001-2, REQ-003-2, REQ-029, REQ-035-2, REQ-036-2, REQ-050)_
- **link_purchase_order_business_entity** — connects hub_purchase_order, hub_business_entity. Declared foreign key PurchaseOrderHeader.EmployeeID references BUSINESSENTITYID; ratified from the source catalogue (WP34). _(requirements: —)_

### Satellites (9)

- **sat_business_entity_vendor_details** — on hub_business_entity; payload: AccountNumber, Name, PurchasingWebServiceURL. Vendor identification and descriptive details: account number, company name and the optional purchasing web service address. Source table: Vendor. Split rationale: Identifying details that rarely change, kept apart from the commercial status codes that change more often.. _(requirements: REQ-002, REQ-004, REQ-011, REQ-012)_
- **sat_business_entity_vendor_status** — on hub_business_entity; payload: CreditRating, PreferredVendorStatus, ActiveFlag, ModifiedDate. Vendor credit rating, preferred status and active flag, with history kept so the vendor's state at order time can be reconstructed. Source table: Vendor. Split rationale: Coded status attributes that change faster and whose history is explicitly required. Holds the single ModifiedDate for the Vendor source.. _(requirements: REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-009, REQ-013, REQ-014, REQ-037-2, REQ-040-2)_
- **sat_product_vendor_terms** — on link_product_vendor; payload: AverageLeadTime, StandardPrice, MinOrderQty, MaxOrderQty, ModifiedDate. Standing commercial terms agreed for a product from a vendor: lead time, standard price and order quantity bounds. History is kept for trend analysis. Source table: ProductVendor. Split rationale: Agreed terms that change slowly. Holds the single ModifiedDate for ProductVendor.. _(requirements: REQ-018, REQ-019, REQ-022, REQ-023, REQ-027, REQ-030-2, REQ-009-2, REQ-019-2, REQ-037-2)_
- **sat_product_vendor_receipt** — on link_product_vendor; payload: LastReceiptCost, LastReceiptDate, OnOrderQty. Running purchasing figures for the supply relationship: last receipt cost and date, and quantity currently on order. Source table: ProductVendor. Split rationale: Running values that change with each order or receipt, much faster than the agreed terms.. _(requirements: REQ-020, REQ-021, REQ-024, REQ-028, REQ-018-2)_
- **sat_purchase_order_status** — on hub_purchase_order; payload: Status, RevisionNumber, ModifiedDate. Purchase order status and revision number, with history kept so status transitions and revisions can be traced. Source table: PurchaseOrderHeader. Split rationale: Workflow attributes that change with each revision or status transition. Holds the single ModifiedDate for PurchaseOrderHeader.. _(requirements: REQ-040, REQ-041, REQ-042, REQ-043, REQ-044, REQ-045, REQ-046, REQ-047, REQ-037-2)_
- **sat_purchase_order_details** — on hub_purchase_order; payload: OrderDate, ShipDate, SubTotal, TaxAmt, Freight, TotalDue. Purchase order dates and financial totals: order date, estimated ship date, subtotal, tax, freight and total due. Source table: PurchaseOrderHeader. Split rationale: Order dates and monetary totals, split from the workflow status attributes.. _(requirements: REQ-037, REQ-038, REQ-039, REQ-048, REQ-049, REQ-050, REQ-051, REQ-052, REQ-039-2)_
- **sat_purchase_order_line_details** — on hub_purchase_order_line; payload: DueDate, OrderQty, UnitPrice, LineTotal. Ordered terms of a purchase order line: due date, ordered quantity, unit price and line total. Source table: PurchaseOrderDetail. Split rationale: Terms fixed when the order is placed, which rarely change afterwards.. _(requirements: REQ-004-2, REQ-005-2, REQ-006-2, REQ-007-2, REQ-008-2, REQ-009-2, REQ-017-2, REQ-050)_
- **sat_purchase_order_line_receipt** — on hub_purchase_order_line; payload: ReceivedQty, RejectedQty, StockedQty, ModifiedDate. Cumulative received, rejected and accepted (stocked) quantities per line. History is kept so the quantity received as at a date, and partial deliveries, are visible. Source table: PurchaseOrderDetail. Split rationale: Receipt progression that changes with each delivery. Holds the single ModifiedDate for PurchaseOrderDetail.. _(requirements: REQ-010-2, REQ-011-2, REQ-012-2, REQ-013-2, REQ-014-2, REQ-015-2, REQ-016-2, REQ-034-2, REQ-037-2)_
- **sat_ship_method_details** — on hub_ship_method; payload: Name, ShipBase, ShipRate, ModifiedDate. Shipping company name and agreed ship base and ship rate, with history kept so historical freight can be checked against the rates then in force. The rowguid replication identifier is left out. Source table: ShipMethod. _(requirements: REQ-021-2, REQ-023-2, REQ-024-2, REQ-025-2, REQ-026-2, REQ-027-2, REQ-028-2)_
